title: What lives in the deepest ocean?
sources: Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution Hadal Organisms

lines.text: In the Mariana Trench, where pressure would crush a steel submarine, what bizarre creatures actually survive?
Under crushing pressure and freezing darkness, life has adapted in terrifying ways.
The Mariana snailfish lives five miles deep, having completely scaleless gelatinous tissue to resist pressure.
lines.caps: The snailfish has *gelatinous skin | and soft flexible *bones

lines.text: Giant amphipods grow to the size of dinner plates, feeding on dead whale carcasses sinking from above.
lines.caps: Giant amphipods *grow | to the size of *dinner plates!

lines.text: Deep sea anglerfish illuminate pitch black waters with glowing bioluminescent bacterial lures on their foreheads.
lines.caps: Anglerfish use *bioluminescent lures | to bait unsuspecting *prey

lines.text: Many deep-sea animals don't have eyes at all, navigating by sensing water pressure vibrations.
lines.caps: Many creatures have *no eyes | relying purely on vibration *sensors

lines.text: The bottom of our ocean feels closer to another planet than planet Earth.
lines.caps: The deep abyss feels *closer | to an alien *planet!
